title: Acha bar Chadya, Who Was Called Aya Mari
author: Aharon Hyman
attribution: Model-assisted translation, editorially reviewed; publication authorized by Joshua Waxman.

paragraphs: He is mentioned in Gittin 35a, but he is not one of the sages, only a man so named who divorced his wife. In Rabbeinu Chananel’s commentary there, at 34b, the reading is Rav Acha bar Chavira, who was called Abba bar Mari.[^1][^2]

notes.text: The William Davidson digital Gittin 35a spells the name אחא בר הידיא דמתקרי איה מרי; the supplied heading has חדייא / אייא מרי. The Rabbeinu Chananel form is Hyman’s report, not a newly inspected commentary reading.

The checked Gittin 35a passage names Acha bar Hidya, called Aya Mari, in the divorce formula, beside the supplied Chadya/Aya Mari forms. The Rabbeinu Chananel reading at 34b remains Hyman’s report: that commentary passage was unavailable in the bounded retrieval and has not been directly collated. No title or personal identity is transferred between these forms.
